cards.note: "I at birth" and "Nates" transcribed as printed (evident OCR/print defects for "If at birth" and "Notes"); "Neechabhang" (no final "a") likewise transcribed as printed, the only one of the five verses to spell it that way. INTERPRETIVE STEP TAKEN AND RECORDED: the verse's own "or" (this card's condition, disjunctive) is corroborated by the Note immediately following v.26 (not quoted by this card; see PD.07.Neechabhanga.UchchanathaNote), where the translator explicitly adopts "any of the two conditions should be enough" against a named dissenting view (Pt. Gopesh Kumar Ojha) requiring both. The same Note's worked example (Saturn debilitated in Aries; Mars, Aries's own lord, and Sun, exalted in Aries, both in Kendra to the Lagna) confirms "the planet that is exalted in the sign" means the graha whose OWN exaltation sign is the debilitated planet's depression sign -- Mars in the example, Sun in the other -- not a further lordship lookup, and directly validates this card's per-graha table. Moon's branch carries only its debilitation-sign lord (Mars): no classical graha among Sun-Saturn exalts in Scorpio, and Mantreswara's own chapter 1 is silent on Rahu/Ketu's exaltation (PD.01.Exaltation.RahuKetu.Mantreswara), so the second disjunct has no doctrine to test for the Moon and is correctly omitted rather than guessed. Venus's branch collapses to its single debilitation-sign lord (Mercury) because Mercury also exalts in Virgo, Venus's own debilitation sign -- both disjuncts name the same graha. The Neechabhanga family (vv.26-30) is Chapter 7 slice 1 (Milestone 36); verses 1-25 are individually deferred in Rules/deferred.json, none silently dropped. source.quote: Note — There is some difference of opinion about the interpretation of the word Uchchanatha. Suppose Saturn is in the Aries in debilitation who will be Uchchanatha of Saturn? According to one view Saturn is exalted in Libra. Therefore lord of Libra, namely, Venus is the Uchchanatha. Another view is that Saturn being in Aries and the Sun is exalted in Aries. Therefore the Sun is the Uchchanatha. In our view the second view is more appropriate. There is also difference of opinion whether the conditions mentioned above have to be fulfilled before debilitation gets cancelled. Shri V. Subrahmanaya Shastri has taken the view that any of the two conditions should be enough for the cancellation of the debilitation. Pt. Gopesh Kumar Ojha has taken the view that both the conditions have to be fulfilled. We are of the view that it should be enough for any of the two conditions to be fulfilled for the cancellation of the debilitation. Our view and that of Shri Shastri is supported by Jataka Parijata.
